newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Financial says to meet profit goal.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Financial says to meet profit goal.

text.p: Pioneer Financial Services Inc said Monday it was on track to meet its profit goal for the year.
It did not specify its goal but said analysts' earnings estimates for the year range from $2 to $2.05 per fully diluted share.
In 1995 Pioneer Financial earned $1.85 per diluted share, with operating income of $1.91 per diluted share.
Pioneer, an insurance underwriter and marketer, said the Kassebaum-Kennedy federal healthcare reform legislation passed recently is expected to affect its group medical and senior health divisions.

"In mid-November we are introducing to our national sales forces Medical Savings Account (MSA) plans for small business owners and the self-emnployed," Peter Nauert, chairman, said in a statement. The MSA plans are expected to generate "significant interest" in selected markets in 1997, he added.
Pioneer today reported earnings of $0.52 per fully diluted share for the third quarter, up from $0.30 a year ago.

"Our earnings continued to be consistent with our expectations," Nauert said. "Through our recent strategic acquisitions, we reached a number of important milestones during the quarter. We now have annualized revenue of approximately $1 billion and we expect that total assets will closely approach $2 billion by year-end."
